reviewers.agent: claude general-purpose subagent, independent context; three rounds over the branch and each fix delta, given the engine:claude rule bodies verbatim (blank-line-after-block included, now that it is declared), the skills-policy charter and a warden-packaged diff. Reviews executed rather than read: the scanner was run against constructed markdown, the four README wiki URLs were resolved against a page set derived from docPages/pageName rather than the live wiki, and the test-cache hazard was reproduced for the new scanner in a scratch repo.

claude general-purpose subagent, separate context; every round refuted its own findings before reporting and returned an explicit refuted list — among them the emoji typography question, Home handling shared with the nav test, the docs/internal mirroring claim, and whether the wiki-sync path filter undercuts 'regenerated on every push to main'. A full eight-mutation kill matrix was run against the eleven table cases, confirming no survivor.

records.finding: [r1] The new test was inserted between TestThisRepoNavigationCoversEveryPage's doc comment and its function, so the comment documented a test that does none of what it says and the nav test was left uncommented.
records.evidence: Two adjacent comment blocks with no function between them; the described function sat 80 lines below, uncommented.
records.reason: Moved below the nav test. This is the second time in one session I made this exact insertion error — the first was TestExtractFences in test/docsnippets.

records.finding: [r1] The scanner was not markdown-aware and would fail the build on correct links: the page-name class swallowed a trailing sentence period, and unlike every other scanner in the module it did not skip fenced blocks.
records.evidence: Appending `See .../wiki/adapters.` and a fenced `curl .../wiki/some-page` to a doc made the real test fail on both. main.go's linkTargets skips fences precisely so a fenced example does not count as a link.
records.reason: Extracted as wikiPageRefs, which skips fences and trims the trailing period. A sentence-ending URL was confirmed not to fail after the fix.

records.finding: [r1] The anti-vacuity floor counted URLs seen rather than pages resolved: the counter incremented before the bare-wiki-root `continue`, so root links, validated against nothing, satisfied it.
records.evidence: Deleting the four page links from README left the test passing on two root links while resolving no page at all.
records.reason: Counts pages actually checked. Reinstating the old counter reddens the guard itself.

records.finding: [r1] The new matching logic had no table-driven cases and was exercised only by whatever URLs README happened to contain, with its edge behaviour wrong in exactly the cases a table would have listed.
records.evidence: Every other pure helper in the module is table-driven, including TestRewriteSkipsCodeFences — the fence case the new scanner got wrong.
records.reason: Eleven subtests over an extracted wikiPageRefs; a mutation matrix of eight distinct mutations leaves no subtest unkilled.

records.finding: [r1] The source list hardcoded three files, leaving adapters/README.md, SECURITY.md and .github/ outside the guard with nothing to say so.
records.evidence: The comment claimed to list 'the docs that may carry absolute wiki URLs' while four tracked .md files were excluded.
records.reason: Walks every tracked .md, with its own floor.

records.finding: [r2] The table written to prove the scanner non-vacuous was itself vacuous: asserting with strings.Join cannot distinguish nil from [""], so the two subtests pinning the wiki-root guard could not detect its loss.
records.evidence: Deleting `if page == "" { continue }` left all ten subtests green; `return nil` reddened only six of ten.
records.reason: slices.Equal compares length and elements; both root cases now redden on exactly that mutation.

records.finding: [r2] wikiPageRefs skipped fenced blocks but not inline code spans while its doc comment claimed parity with every other scanner in the module. A wiki URL shown inside backticks would have failed the required core-checks job.
records.evidence: wikiPageRefs on 'run `curl .../wiki/not-a-page` to fetch' returned the page. linkTargets and rewriteLine both split on the backtick first.
records.reason: Splits on the backtick, byte-identically to linkTargets. A named case reddens when the even-segment step is removed.

records.finding: [r2] The doc comment justifying the whole test cited an 'in-repo link checker' that only follows relative paths. No link checker exists anywhere in this tree.
records.evidence: grep for link-check mechanisms across workflows, scripts, Go and markdown returns only the sentence itself. The relative-link checking had been an ad-hoc shell one-liner run during review, written up as though it were a repo artifact — ADR-0008 clause 3.
records.reason: The comment says what is true: nothing here would notice, and rewriteSegment leaves an unresolvable target as written rather than inventing a destination.

records.finding: [r2] The comment paying for the -count=1 cost enumerated the whole-tree git ls-files scanners as three; trackedMarkdown makes test/wikisync a fourth with the same cache exposure.
records.evidence: Reproduced for the new scanner: an unlisted doc gave `ok (cached)` while -count=1 failed naming it.
records.reason: All four named. An ALL-CAPS emphasis left in that comment earlier was removed at the same time.

records.finding: [r3] The comment explaining the assertion credited the wrong artifact: '%q rather than Join' names the Errorf verb, which has no effect on pass or fail. The mechanism is slices.Equal on the adjacent line.
records.evidence: With the root guard deleted, both root subtests fail under slices.Equal; the verb is not load-bearing.
records.reason: States the constraint the comparison must satisfy.

records.finding: [r3] The comment's content was an argument against the previous commit's implementation. strings.Join appears nowhere in the file, so a fresh reader has no prior version to weigh it against and it reads as persuasion aimed at this diff's reviewer.
records.evidence: ADR-0014 lists change history and persuasion under 'Never in comments'; the review corpus carries a judged finding of the same shape in adapters/export/otlp/pipeline_test.go.
records.reason: Rewritten as a constraint: nil and [""] must not compare equal, because the wiki-root cases pin a guard whose loss turns the first into the second.
